title: The ark in full
hook: Nuh builds, the waters come, and the ark sails in Allah's name (11:37–41)
carry: in his name it sails and anchors

segments.voice: Yesterday: Hud, the surah that turned him gray. Your line was weighty words. Today ends a week.

This week opened Block B: the friends of God, with no fear and no grief; Pharaoh's right words too late, and a whole town's just in time; the question, would you compel them; and why Hud turned the Prophet's hair gray. Now Hud's first long story. Last year you watched Nuh build on dry land while the neighbors laughed, and call to his son on the mountain. Today, the voyage itself, start to finish, because Surah Hud gives it a shape, and a single line people still say when they set out.
screen: `A WEEK: FEAR, TOO LATE, IN TIME.`

segments.voice: It begins with a command, in verse thirty-seven: build the ship under Our eyes and by Our inspiration. Bi-a'yunina: under Our eyes. Every plank laid while being watched over. Then the sign comes, water gushing out, and the order: load on it a pair of every kind, your household, and those who believe. And the verse adds, almost quietly: and they were only a few. Then Nuh speaks, in Pickthall's translation: "Embark therein! In the name of Allah be its course and its mooring." Bismillahi majraha wa mursaha. Majra is the sailing, the running of the ship; mursa is the anchoring, the coming to rest. Both in God's name: the going and the stopping. Some Muslims still say these words when they board a boat or set out on a journey. The middle of the voyage is the hard part: waves like mountains, and the son who would not come aboard. Then the ending, in verse forty-four, in a run of short commands. Earth, swallow your water. Sky, hold back. The water sinks away, the command is fulfilled, the ship comes to rest on al-Judi. And in verse forty-eight, the last word to Nuh: go down, in peace from Us, and with blessings on you and on the peoples who will come from those with you. Read in full, the voyage has three parts. It sets out in God's name. It comes to rest in God's name. And it steps off in peace.
screen: `BUILD IT UNDER OUR EYES.` · `AND THEY WERE ONLY A FEW.` · `IN GOD'S NAME, ITS COURSE AND MOORING.` · `EARTH, SWALLOW; SKY, HOLD BACK.` · then, large: `IN HIS NAME IT SAILS AND ANCHORS.`

segments.voice: Think of the next journey you'll take, even a small one, the drive to work or the walk to the store, and picture the moment you set off and the moment you arrive. If you pray, you can say Nuh's words at both ends: in God's name its course, in God's name its mooring. If not, simply give the start and the stop a breath of attention.
Al-Judi. The mountain where Nuh's ark came to rest, after God's command: earth, swallow your water; sky, hold back. Today's word.
Your line: in his name it sails and anchors. The going and the stopping, both in God's name. A week of Block B, done.

howItsDone: Some Muslims recite Nuh's words from 11:41, bismillahi majraha wa mursaha, when boarding a ship or setting out on a journey, alongside the traveler's supplication taught in the hadith.
